full_judgment:
3. Plaintiffs' case, in short, is that the suit land was originally belonged to Jagadish Chandra Sen and others. Thereafter Jagadish Chandra Sen died leaving behind two sons namely Nirmal Chandra Sen and Parimal Chandra Sen. Aforesaid Nirmal Chandra Sen and Parimal Chandra Sen transferred the suit land to Sahaj Uddin Mia, the father of the plaintiffs by way of pattan on 28th Chaitra 1355 B.S. Then Sahaj Uddin Mia died leaving behind the plaintiffs. On 24.4.1994 when he went to the Tahsil Office for paying land taxes there from bee was informed that the suit land already recorded as vested property. He was further informed that R.S. Parcha was published in the name of the defendant No.1 instead the name of plaintiffs father Sahaj Uddin Mia. The defendants have no right, title and possession over the suit land. The plaintiff was and is in possession of the suit land. The publication of S.A. and R.S. Parcha has clouded the title of the plaintiffs. Then the plaintiffs filed the instant suit praying for declaration of title over the suit property and correction of the records. 

 5. The case of the defendant No.1 in short is that, originally the land was belonged to one Jagadish Chandra Sen, who died leaving behind two sons namely Nirmal Chandra Sen and Parimal Chandra Sen. Subsequently aforesaid Nirmal Chandra Sen and Parimal Chandra Sen transferred the suit property to the defendant's father by way of pattan. 

 15. It further appears from the deposition of P.W.3 Khorshed Mia who deposed supporting the plaintiffs' case. He stated that the plaintiffs are possessing ½  decimal of land and the defendant did not possess any land. In cross-examination he stated that Sahaj Uddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs possessed the land at least 37/38 years. He also denied the suggestion that defendant No.1 took pattan of the land from the C.S. recorded tenant Parimal. P.W.4 Mahmudul Islam also deposed supporting the plaintiffs' case. He stated in his cross-examination that, “আমি বাদীদের অধীনে ভাড়া থাকি, চুক্তিপত্র আছে। চুক্তিপত্র দাখিল করি নাই। আমার ভাড়ার কোন রশিদ আজ আনি নাই। আমার আগে না ঘরে মহিউদ্দিন ব্যবসা করিত। সুতার ব্যবসা করিত। আমার বাড়ী বাগহাটা বাদীর বাড়ীর কাছাকাছি।” This witness supports the plaintiffs' case and the possession of the suit property. The appellate Court without reversing the depositions of the P.Ws 1-3 he only disbelieved the hokum nama of both the plaintiffs as well as defendant and allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. He apparently failed to follow the Order 41 rule 31 of the C.P.C. that is reversed the judgment of the trial Court without controverting the finding of the trial court.
